message.content:
Yes—you can file a noise complaint with the City of Atlanta’s local authorities.  
Here’s how:

| Step | What to do | Where / How |
|------|------------|-------------|
| **1** | **Check the city’s noise ordinance** – Atlanta’s ordinance defines what constitutes “excessive noise” and the hours it applies. | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/departments/department-of-public-safety/police-department/code-enforcement/noise-ordinance> |
| **2** | **File an online complaint** – Use the City’s 311 portal to submit a noise complaint. | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311/noise-complaint> |
| **3** | **Call the non‑emergency police line** – If you prefer to speak directly or the situation isn’t urgent. | 404‑656‑4000 (non‑emergency) |
| **4** | **Email the Noise Enforcement Unit** – For written records or if you’re unable to use the online form. | noise@cityofatlanta.org |
| **5** | **Visit City Hall** – If you need to speak in person or have documentation to submit. | 1000 Peachtree Street NW, Atlanta, GA 30303 |

### Quick Tips

* **Time of day matters** – Most ordinances prohibit loud noises after 10 p.m. on weekdays and 11 p.m. on weekends.  
* **Provide details** – Include the location, time, type of noise, and any evidence (photos, videos, audio recordings).  
* **Follow up** – After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. Keep it handy if you need to check status or provide additional information.

If the noise is an emergency (e.g., a fire alarm, a threat of violence), dial **911** immediately. Otherwise, the above channels will route your complaint to the appropriate city department for investigation and enforcement.
